audit.why: 51.07% over 3313 games with a FAVOURED 4/10 rating is defensible: Talon owns a real level-3 kill window, and after 6 Frozen Tomb's untargetable self-cast answers a burst assassin who must stand next to you to finish the Blade's End bleed.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..3].side all read Lissandra while content win[0..3] read Skill — four rows rendering two different answers. packet.levelChart matches the content layer.
audit.why: Before 6 Lissandra has no answer to a committed W-Q all-in except a 24s-cooldown E, and Rake at 650 out-ranges her W at 450, so levels 1-5 are genuinely skill. The Lissandra rows are correct only from 6 onward, where they already sit.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> Skill, each why rewritten in the same proposal to describe an even stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: no Talon ability was named anywhere, and breakdown.cooldowns held no digit. Two interactions that decide the lane were absent: Noxian Diplomacy refunding its own cooldown on a kill, and Assassin's Path putting the terrain it used on a long cooldown while Lissandra's E crosses any wall freely.
audit.why: Riot's text: Noxian Diplomacy 'refunds some health and cooldown if this ability kills the target' — so a Talon who gets a kill in a chase has his 8s Q immediately. Assassin's Path 'has a low cooldown, but puts the used terrain on a long cooldown' — the wall he escaped over is not available to him twice, and Lissandra's E ignores that restriction entirely.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, ahead and dontsFull[2].d with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Whether Lissandra's W (a no-target AoE root around her) hits Talon while he is Invisible during Shadow Assault is not answerable from the kit file.
audit.why: Riot's text says Talon 'becomes Invisible'; Ring of Frost's text says it freezes 'nearby enemies'. Whether an invisible unit is a legal AoE target is exactly the kind of thing the brief says the kit file cannot settle, so I asserted nothing about it.
audit.corrected: No claim written; escalated in questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under 'Self-R his burst, then W-Q the counter'; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Chase resets past your claw range'. dontsFull[0].d was a name-swappable template.
audit.why: Each title promised something the body never explained.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten to their own titles using Rake's 650 range, the Q leap's 575, and the Q cooldown refund.

edits.before: Q-shatter the wave and chip his melee step-ups — your early Q harass is better than the lane gives it credit for.
edits.after: Even level 1: he has no leap without a target for Noxian Diplomacy, and your Q at 725 outranges his 575 stab.

edits.before: W online: anyone who closes onto you eats a root. The anti-engage layer is already real at level 2.
edits.after: Still even — W roots him inside 450, but Rake reaches 650 and chips you without ever entering it.

edits.before: E claw completes the kit — you now have the lane's strangest engage and a guaranteed exit. Greed carefully; the claw is slow.
edits.after: Skill: his W-Q all-in at level 3 is a real kill window, and your E at 1050 is the only thing that answers it — keep it as an exit.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q spam stops hurting your mana. Chip Talon every time he touches the wave.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies your mana; Talon still has a kill if you step past the wave with E down.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. It governs your forward steps. - R Frozen Tomb (self-cast) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and 7s at rank 5, reaches 650, and the returning blades carry most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. - Noxian Diplomacy is 8s and refunds its cooldown on a kill. - Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Talon wins by stacking Blade's End with Rake, then Q-leaping in for the bleed before your W comes back.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Q him at 725 while he holds Rake, and the moment his Q leap lands inside 450, W-root and rotate — he has to re-approach with nothing left.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Clawing in while Rake is up — the daggers slow you on the return and Blade's End bleeds while you stand there with no exit for 24s.

edits.before: Good trade: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive. Bad trade: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Good trade: Q him at 725 while he holds Rake, and the moment his Q leap lands inside 450, W-root and rotate — he re-approaches with nothing. Bad trade: clawing in while Rake is up, where the daggers slow you on the return and Blade's End bleeds you while your exit sits on a 24s cooldown.

edits.before: Carry through picks — claw-root-tomb converts vision into kills better than any control mage; the map shrinks every time your E is up.
edits.after: Carry by owning the flanks — Assassin's Path burns each wall as he uses it, while your E crosses any wall on a 12s cooldown at rank 5.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt: claw into every river skirmish first, tomb the carry, and snowball picks — Talon farming under tower can't stop a roaming Lissandra.
edits.after: Ahead, hunt: he cannot vault the same wall twice in a row, so cut the terrain he escaped over, tomb him there, and take the pick.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Self-R as his Shadow Assault blades converge — you surface untargetable and healed, then W-root him inside 450 and Q before Blade's End bleeds.

edits.before: That’s Talon’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Rake reaches 650 and his Q leap needs 575 — hold W for the leap, not the daggers.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Noxian Diplomacy refunds its cooldown on a kill, so a chased Talon gets his 8s Q straight back and vaults a wall you followed him past.

notes: phases[0..3].side read Lissandra against content win[0..3] = Skill (which matches packet.levelChart); I moved the full layer onto the content values, so there is no paired win[N] edit to write — the content values are already the targets. All four whys were rewritten in the same proposal to match the Skill verdict. phases[4..6] already agreed across layers and were left alone. No lint findings on report[] and none of the report entries name a fabricated ability, so report[] was untouched per the sweep exclusion. Talon's E cooldown is listed as 0 in the kit with the caveat that the used terrain goes on a long cooldown; I wrote the caveat, not a '0 second dash', since the raw number would mislead.
